Validation

validate.Rmd

The purpose of validation is to ensure that the input datasets required for aggregation are in the correct format. The primary function for validation is validate_input_data(). This function is called automatically when you run aggregate_data(), so it is not necessary to perform validation manually. However, running validation separately before aggregation is useful for catching data issues early, especially when working with large datasets.

What is checked

Validation covers four main areas:

Person data

  • All required columns are present (PID, DOB, SEX) and optional columns (ENROL_DATE, CENSOR_DATE, CENSOR_TYPE) are correctly typed if present
  • PID values are unique (no duplicate persons)
  • Date columns (DOB, ENROL_DATE, CENSOR_DATE) are stored as 8-digit integers in yyyymmdd format
  • Date consistency: DOB ≤ ENROL_DATE ≤ CENSOR_DATE
  • CENSOR_TYPE values are from the allowed set ("missing", "dead", "travelled", "emigrated")
  • At least some persons are active during the cycle period

Vaccination data (skipped if vaccination_data = NULL)

  • All required columns are present (PID, V_DATE, V_SUBTYPE) and correctly typed
  • All PID values exist in person_data
  • V_DATE is in valid 8-digit integer format
  • V_SUBTYPE codes match those defined in the options file
  • Vaccination dates fall within each person’s active period (after ENROL_DATE, before CENSOR_DATE)

Outcome data

  • All required columns are present (PID, AESI, EVENT_DATE, ENCOUNTER_TYPE) and correctly typed
  • All PID values exist in person_data
  • AESI codes match those defined in the options file
  • EVENT_DATE is in valid 8-digit integer format
  • Event dates fall within each person’s active period

Lookback coverage

Checks that outcome data extends far enough back before the first vaccination (or cycle start, for historical aggregation) to satisfy the lookback requirement. By default, at least 75% of the configured lookback period (default: 2 years) must be covered. If insufficient coverage is detected, an interactive prompt allows you to provide a custom lookback start date to confirm awareness of the limitation.

Return value

validate_input_data() returns a character vector of issue descriptions. An empty vector means no issues were found and the data is ready for aggregation. When issues are present, each entry describes a specific problem to address.

issues <- validate_input_data(person_data, vaccination_data, outcome_data,
                              cycle_start_date = as.Date("2022-01-01"),
                              cycle_end_date = as.Date("2022-01-31"))

if (length(issues) == 0) {
  message("No issues found.")
} else {
  print(issues)
}

Options file

validate_input_data() reads the same options.txt file as aggregate_data() — it uses this to check that vaccine subtype codes and AESI codes in the input data match those defined for the study. The options_file_location parameter specifies the folder containing options.txt and defaults to the current working directory (getwd()). You can also supply a pre-parsed options object directly via the options parameter (see ?read_options_file).

Set up for examples

Load the package:

library(rapidcycler)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)

If you would like to use synthetic data to run the examples, you can create and save that in the current working directory with the code below:

generate_synthetic_data(pop_size = 1000000)

Or, if you already have some data saved in the current working directory, load it as so:

person_data <- data.table::fread("person_data.csv")
vaccination_data <- data.table::fread("vaccination_data.csv")
outcome_data <- data.table::fread("outcome_data.csv")

Example: Valid input data 

# options.txt is assumed to be in the current working directory
validate_input_data(person_data, vaccination_data, outcome_data,
                    cycle_start_date = as.Date("2022-01-01"),
                    cycle_end_date = as.Date("2022-01-31"))
# Returns character(0) — no issues found

To specify a different location for the options file:

validate_input_data(person_data, vaccination_data, outcome_data,
                    cycle_start_date = as.Date("2022-01-01"),
                    cycle_end_date = as.Date("2022-01-31"),
                    options_file_location = "~/Documents/RCA_COVID/")

Example: Invalid input data

The example below introduces three deliberate errors: an incorrect column type for DOB, a renamed vaccination date column, and an unrecognised AESI code. The returned vector will describe each issue.

issues <- validate_input_data(
  person_data %>% mutate(DOB = as.character(DOB)),       # DOB should be integer, not character
  vaccination_data %>% rename(VAC_DATE = V_DATE),        # V_DATE column missing
  outcome_data %>% mutate(AESI = if_else(AESI == "ADEM", "ADM", AESI)), # unrecognised AESI code
  cycle_start_date = as.Date("2022-01-01"),
  cycle_end_date = as.Date("2022-01-31")
)
print(issues)

Example: Historical input data

When vaccination_data = NULL, vaccination-related checks are skipped. This is used when aggregating data from a period before the vaccination campaign began.

validate_input_data(person_data,
                    vaccination_data = NULL,
                    outcome_data,
                    cycle_start_date = as.Date("2022-01-01"),
                    cycle_end_date = as.Date("2022-01-31"))
